```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tinyAM)
guide_root <- Sys.getenv("TINYAM_GUIDE_ROOT")
source_files <- if (nzchar(guide_root)) {
  c(file.path("R", list.files(file.path(guide_root, "R"), "[.]R$")), "NAMESPACE")
} else {
  list.files(system.file("R", package = "tinyAM"), full.names = TRUE)
}
source_hashes <- tools::md5sum(if (nzchar(guide_root)) {
  file.path(guide_root, source_files)
} else source_files)
versions <- c(tinyAM = as.character(packageVersion("tinyAM")),
  R = as.character(getRversion()), RTMB = as.character(packageVersion("RTMB")),
  mgcv = as.character(packageVersion("mgcv")))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  cache.extra = list(versions = versions, sources = unname(source_hashes), inputs = cod_obs))
```

When fish are scarce, a catch or survey sample can record zero for an age
even if fish of that age are present. The default lognormal family uses
positive observations. The Poisson-link delta (PLD) families also use
recorded zeros to inform the predicted catch or index. Thorson's Poisson-link
model uses a shared quantity to explain both encounter probability and the
size of positive observations. tinyAM links both to the assessment's predicted
catch or index. [Thorson (2018)](https://repository.library.noaa.gov/view/noaa/54874) ·
[sdmTMB Poisson-link delta guide](https://sdmtmb.github.io/sdmTMB/articles/poisson-link.html)

## The observation model

Let \(Y\) be a recorded catch or index and \(\widetilde Y\) the predicted
arithmetic mean across zeros and positives. Each survey or fleet has one
detection scale \(\widetilde Y_{50}\), in the same units as the prediction.

\[
p_0 = P(Y=0) = 2^{-\widetilde Y/\widetilde Y_{50}},
\qquad
E[Y\mid Y>0] = \frac{\widetilde Y}{1-p_0}.
\]

When the predicted catch or index equals \(\widetilde Y_{50}\), half the
observations are expected to be zero. Doubling the prediction lowers that
probability to 25%. The positive mean is larger than the overall mean because
it averages only observations above zero. The positive component models the
spread around that mean. Use `pld_lognormal()`, `pld_gamma()`, or
`pld_gengamma()` to specify its distribution. Each uses the same equation for
encounter probability.
[Observation family reference](../reference/observation_families.html)

## Apply PLD to Northern cod

```{r zero-counts, include=FALSE}
years <- 1983:2025
ages <- 2:20
zero_count <- function(x) sum(x$obs == 0 & x$year %in% years & x$age %in% ages,
  na.rm = TRUE)
```

Northern cod has **`r zero_count(cod_obs$catch)` recorded catch zeros** and
**`r zero_count(cod_obs$index)` Fall 2J3KL survey zeros** at ages 2–20+ in
1983–2025. We fit two observation families to this case, the default
lognormal and the Poisson-link delta lognormal.

```{r fits, cache=TRUE, results="hide"}
ncam <- fit_tam(cod_obs, years = 1983:2025, ages = 2:20,
  N_settings = list(process = "off", init = "exp"),
  rec_settings = list(process = "rw"),
  F_settings = list(process = "ar1", mu_form = ~ 1, mean_ages = 5:14),
  M_settings = list(process = "ar1", mu_supplied = ~ I(0.3),
    age_breaks = c(2, 5, 8, 21), mean_ages = 5:14),
  catch_settings = list(sd_form = ~ 1),
  index_settings = list(sd_form = ~ 1, q_form = ~ mono(q_block)),
  silent = TRUE
)

ncam_pld <- update(ncam,
  catch_settings = list(family = pld_lognormal()),
  index_settings = list(family = pld_lognormal()),
  silent = TRUE
)
```

The lognormal fit treats recorded zeros as missing in the likelihood.
Under PLD, a recorded zero contributes the fitted probability of observing
zero. Truly missing observations contribute to neither likelihood. The
lognormal model predicts a median for the positive observations. PLD
predicts an arithmetic mean across zeros and positives.

### Half-detection levels

```{r detection-scales, echo=FALSE}
scales <- subset(tidy_par(ncam_pld)$fixed, par %in% c("y50_catch", "y50_index"))
scales$series <- ifelse(scales$par == "y50_catch", "Commercial catch", "Fall 2J3KL survey")
knitr::kable(scales[c("series", "est", "lwr", "upr", "unit")], digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c("Series", "Detection scale", "Lower 95%", "Upper 95%", "Units"))
```

For each series, a fitted mean near its half-detection level gives a zero
probability near 50%. The table uses the same units as the matrices below.

### Which observations are likely to be zero?

The numbers in the cells are the observations, in thousands of fish. The
colour shows the probability of zero calculated from the fitted mean. Darker
cells have higher probabilities. Grey cells mark missing observations. Hover
over a cell for the full recorded value, fitted mean, and probability. In the
cell labels, `k` means one thousand of the displayed units.

```{r observation-matrices, echo=FALSE}
d <- tidy_obs_pred(ncam_pld)
observation_matrix <- function(data, title) {
  cells <- expand.grid(year = years, age = ages)
  key <- match(paste(cells$year, cells$age), paste(data$year, data$age))
  observed <- data$obs[key]
  predicted <- data$pred_mean[key]
  probability <- ifelse(is.na(observed), NA_real_, data$p_zero[key])
  number <- function(x) format(x, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE, digits = 12)
  rounded <- ifelse(observed < 10, formatC(observed, format = "f", digits = 1),
    ifelse(observed < 10000, as.character(round(observed)),
      paste0(round(observed / 1000), "k")))
  cells$label <- ifelse(is.na(observed), "\u2013",
    ifelse(observed == 0, "0", ifelse(observed < 0.1, "<0.1", rounded)))
  age_labels <- as.character(ages)
  age_labels[length(ages)] <- paste0(max(ages), "+")
  age_label <- age_labels[match(cells$age, ages)]
  fitted_values <- paste0("<br>Fitted mean: ", number(predicted),
    " thousand fish<br>Probability of zero: ", sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * probability))
  hover <- paste0("Year: ", cells$year, "<br>Age: ", age_label, "<br>",
    ifelse(is.na(observed), "Observation: missing",
      paste0("Observed: ", number(observed), " thousand fish", fitted_values)))
  cells$dark <- !is.na(probability) & probability >= 0.65
  color_scale <- list(c(0, "#f8fbfd"), c(0.5, "#aacdde"), c(1, "#244f67"))
  p <- plotly::plot_ly(x = ages, y = years,
    z = matrix(probability, nrow = length(years)),
    text = matrix(hover, nrow = length(years)),
    type = "heatmap", colorscale = color_scale, zmin = 0, zmax = 1,
    xgap = 1, ygap = 1, hoverinfo = "text", hoverongaps = FALSE,
    colorbar = list(title = list(text = "Probability<br>of zero"), tickformat = ".0%"),
    height = 850)
  for (on_dark in c(FALSE, TRUE)) {
    p <- plotly::add_text(p, data = cells[cells$dark == on_dark, ],
      x = ~age, y = ~year, text = ~label, hovertext = hover[cells$dark == on_dark],
      hoverinfo = "text", textposition = "middle center", showlegend = FALSE,
      textfont = list(size = 10, color = if (on_dark) "white" else "#15252d"),
      inherit = FALSE)
  }
  p <- plotly::layout(p, title = list(text = paste0(title, " (thousands of fish)")),
    margin = list(t = 105), plot_bgcolor = "#e3e5e8",
    xaxis = list(title = "Age", side = "top", tickvals = ages, ticktext = age_labels,
      showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE, automargin = TRUE),
    yaxis = list(title = "Year", range = c(max(years) + .5, min(years) - .5),
      tickvals = c(1983, seq(1985, 2025, by = 5)), showgrid = FALSE))
  htmltools::div(style = "overflow-x: auto;",
    htmltools::div(style = "min-width: 865px;", plotly::config(p, displayModeBar = FALSE)))
}
observation_matrix(d$catch, "Commercial catch")
observation_matrix(d$index, "Fall 2J3KL survey")
```

Across sampled cells, the fitted probabilities sum to
`r round(sum(d$catch$p_zero[!is.na(d$catch$obs)]))` expected catch zeros and
`r round(sum(d$index$p_zero[!is.na(d$index$obs)]))` expected survey zeros.

## Compare the assessments

```{r sensitivity, include=FALSE, cache=TRUE, dependson="fits"}
ncam14 <- update(ncam, ages = 2:14,
  M_settings = list(age_breaks = c(2, 5, 8, 15)), silent = TRUE)
ncam14_pld <- update(ncam14,
  catch_settings = list(family = pld_lognormal()),
  index_settings = list(family = pld_lognormal()),
  silent = TRUE
)
```

Only six catches and two survey observations are positive at age 20+.
The 20+ estimates therefore draw heavily on the fitted population dynamics.
We also compare the estimated number of fish aged 14 and older. This is a
sum across model ages in the 20+ fits and a single age group in the 14+ fits.
Both abundance plots show point estimates. Shading marks the low-stock years
from 1992 to 2010.

```{r trajectories, echo=FALSE}
fits <- list(Lognormal = ncam, PLD = ncam_pld)
terminal <- stack_list(lapply(fits, function(fit) subset(fit$pop$N, age == 20)),
  label = "model")
older_fish <- function(fit) {
  d <- subset(fit$pop$N, age >= 14)
  stats::aggregate(est ~ year + unit, d, sum)
}
older <- stack_list(lapply(list(
  "Lognormal, fit to 20+" = ncam, "PLD, fit to 20+" = ncam_pld,
  "Lognormal, fit to 14+" = ncam14, "PLD, fit to 14+" = ncam14_pld
), older_fish), label = "model")
ssb <- get_ssb(Lognormal = ncam, PLD = ncam_pld)
terminal_ssb_change <- function(lognormal, pld) {
  last <- function(fit) tail(get_ssb(fit)$est, 1L)
  sprintf("%+.0f%%", 100 * (last(pld) / last(lognormal) - 1))
}
low_stock <- list(type = "rect", xref = "x", yref = "paper",
  x0 = 1992, x1 = 2010, y0 = 0, y1 = 1, layer = "below",
  fillcolor = "rgba(170,205,222,0.3)", line = list(width = 0))
plot_trend(terminal, color = ~model, colors = tam_pal(2),
  ylab = "Age 20+ abundance (thousands of fish)", add_buttons = FALSE,
  add_intervals = FALSE) |>
  plotly::layout(shapes = list(low_stock),
    yaxis = list(type = "log", range = log10(range(terminal$est) * c(0.8, 1.2))))
plot_trend(older, color = ~model, colors = tam_pal(4),
  ylab = "Age 14 and older abundance (thousands of fish)", add_buttons = FALSE) |>
  plotly::layout(shapes = list(low_stock),
    yaxis = list(type = "log", range = log10(range(older$est) * c(0.8, 1.2))))
plot_trend(ssb, color = ~model, colors = tam_pal(2),
  ylab = "Spawning biomass (tonnes)")
```

The log scales make differences visible when abundance was low. For 2025
spawning biomass, the change from lognormal to PLD is
`r terminal_ssb_change(ncam, ncam_pld)` with age 20+ and
`r terminal_ssb_change(ncam14, ncam14_pld)` with age 14+. The size of the
difference depends on the choice of terminal age.

[Northern cod dashboard](../examples/northern-cod-pld/index.html)

## Forecast held-out observations

For each target year from 2006 to 2025, we fit through the previous year
and forecast one year with terminal F held constant. We compare errors
on the same positive survey observations using log-RMSE and MASE.
Both scores use predicted medians for positive observations.
MASE compares pooled absolute errors with using the last available positive
observation as the forecast. Scores below one improve on that baseline.

```{r hindcasts, include=FALSE, cache=TRUE, dependson="fits"}
project <- list(n_proj = 1, n_mean = 1, F_mult = 1)
score_hindcast <- function(Lognormal, PLD, folds) {
  h <- fit_hindcast(Lognormal, PLD = PLD, folds = folds,
    proj_settings = project, progress = FALSE)
  list(index = h$forecast_pairs$index, diagnostics = h$fold_diagnostics,
    occurrence_scores = h$occurrence_scores)
}

paired_survey <- function(hind) {
  d <- hind$index
  if (!nrow(d)) return(d)
  d$log_prediction <- ifelse(d$model == "PLD", d$log_pred_positive, log(d$pred))
  d <- subset(d, is.finite(obs) & obs > 0 & is.finite(log_prediction))
  key <- with(d, interaction(fold, year, age, survey, drop = TRUE))
  d[duplicated(key) | duplicated(key, fromLast = TRUE), ]
}

windows <- list("2006–2025" = score_hindcast(ncam, ncam_pld, folds = 20))
matches <- paired_survey(windows[[1]])
if (sum(matches$age == max(ages) & matches$model == "PLD") < 5L) {
  earlier_lognormal <- update(ncam, years = 1983:2005, silent = TRUE)
  earlier_pld <- update(ncam_pld, years = 1983:2005, silent = TRUE)
  windows[["1992–2005"]] <- score_hindcast(earlier_lognormal, earlier_pld, folds = 14)
}
```

```{r hindcast-scores, echo=FALSE}
scores <- lapply(names(windows), function(window) {
  hind <- windows[[window]]
  matched <- paired_survey(hind)
  diagnostics <- subset(hind$diagnostics, !is_reference)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fits), function(model_name) {
    d <- matched[which(matched$model == model_name), , drop = FALSE]
    attempts <- diagnostics[diagnostics$model == model_name, ]
    data.frame(Window = window, Model = model_name,
      Failed = sum(!attempts$is_converged), Pairs = nrow(d),
      `20+ pairs` = sum(d$age == max(ages)),
      `Log-RMSE` = if (nrow(d)) compute_hindcast_rmse(d) else NA_real_,
      MASE = if (nrow(d)) compute_hindcast_mase(d) else NA_real_,
      check.names = FALSE)
  }))
})
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, scores), digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

The **Pairs** columns count shared positive observations, including how many
were available at age 20+. Both windows had zero matched positives at 20+,
so the positive survey scores evaluate the younger ages. Forecast accuracy at
20+ remains unresolved.

For PLD we can also evaluate the probability of a zero. The Brier score is
the mean squared difference between that probability and the zero indicator.
Smaller values mean better probability forecasts. These scores use all eligible
PLD forecasts, including zeros, and are reported separately by data source.

```{r zero-scores, echo=FALSE}
zero_scores <- lapply(names(windows), function(window) {
  d <- windows[[window]]$occurrence_scores
  if (is.null(d)) return(NULL)
  d <- subset(d, level == "overall" & is.na(horizon))
  data.frame(Window = rep(window, nrow(d)),
    Series = ifelse(d$type == "catch", "Commercial catch", "Fall 2J3KL survey"),
    Observations = d$n, Zeros = d$n_zero, Brier = d$Brier)
})
if (length(Filter(Negate(is.null), zero_scores))) {
  knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, zero_scores), digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
}
```

AIC comparisons require a common likelihood for the same observations.
Here the families use different sets of observations because of the zeros.
Conditional AIC is currently available for the all-lognormal fit only.

## Appendix. Likelihood for a recorded observation

Let \(g_+(z)\) be the density of \(z=\log Y\) conditional on a positive
observation, and let \(p_0=2^{-\widetilde Y/\widetilde Y_{50}}\). A sampled
observation adds the following amount to the log-likelihood.

\[
\ell(Y) =
\begin{cases}
\log p_0, & Y=0,\\
\log(1-p_0)+\log g_+(\log Y), & Y>0.
\end{cases}
\]

Each PLD family sets the arithmetic mean of the positive component to
\(m_+=\widetilde Y/(1-p_0)\). Thus the overall mean is \((1-p_0)m_+=\widetilde Y\).
For PLD lognormal, the conditional distribution of \(\log Y\) is
\(N(\log m_+-\sigma^2/2,\sigma^2)\). The subtraction centres the **arithmetic**
mean of \(Y\) at \(m_+\). For PLD Gamma and generalized Gamma, the
parameters of the positive distribution are likewise set to give mean \(m_+\).
See the family reference for their dispersion and shape parameters.
[Observation family reference](../reference/observation_families.html)

```{r dashboard-export, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
dashboard_cache <- Sys.getenv("TINYAM_PLD_GUIDE_FITS")
if (nzchar(dashboard_cache)) {
  if (!nzchar(guide_root)) stop("Set TINYAM_GUIDE_ROOT to the checkout when exporting guide fits.")
  dir.create(dirname(dashboard_cache), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  saveRDS(list(models = fits, inputs = cod_obs, versions = versions,
    sources = setNames(unname(source_hashes), source_files),
    background = paste(
      "### Northern cod observation families",
      "These NCAM-inspired fits use 1983–2025 and ages 2–20+. The lognormal fit uses positive observations. The PLD fit also uses recorded zeros in both catch and the Fall 2J3KL survey.",
      "See the [Poisson-link delta guide](../../articles/poisson-link-delta.html) for the equations and fitted detection scales.",
      sep = "\n\n")), dashboard_cache)
}
```
